cards.text: Jesus has just gone back and forth with some Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem about eating with unwashed hands (Matthew 15:1-20). Now He leaves that place and withdraws. New road, new district.

cards.question: Jesus leaves the argument about unwashed hands behind. Where does He withdraw to?

answers.text: The district of Tyre and Sidon

cards.text: A Canaanite woman from that region comes to Him. And friend, this is no polite little wave. She's CRYING OUT: "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me!"

cards.question: What's going on that has the Canaanite woman crying out to Jesus for mercy?

answers.text: Her daughter is possessed by a demon
Her husband is sick with a fever
Her son has been blind from birth

cards.question: The Canaanite woman is begging Jesus to help her daughter. Jesus answers her right away.

cards.text: Not one word. Jesus stays silent. So His disciples come over to Him with a suggestion.

cards.question: The disciples urge Jesus to send the Canaanite woman away.
Why do the disciples want Jesus to send the Canaanite woman away?

answers.text: She keeps crying out after them
It is getting late in the day
The crowd is pressing in on them

cards.text: So she's still crying out, and the disciples want her gone. Then Jesus speaks up.

cards.question: Jesus finally speaks. Who does He say He was sent only to?

answers.text: The lost sheep of the house of Israel
The scribes and elders of Jerusalem
The faithful ones in every nation

cards.question: After Jesus says He was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel, the Canaanite woman gives up and heads home.

cards.text: NOPE. She comes and kneels before Him and says, "Lord, help me!"
But Jesus replies, "It is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to the dogs." Now what is she going to say to that?

cards.question: The Canaanite woman answers Jesus' picture of the children's bread and the dogs. She says even the dogs get the ___ that fall from their master's table.

cards.text: She takes the very picture Jesus used and keeps right on asking.
Friend, I've been around cookies my whole life, and crumbs fall EVERY SINGLE BATCH. Then Jesus answers her.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Canaanite woman, "Let it be done for you as you desire."
Jesus grants the Canaanite woman's request. When is her daughter healed?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 17 quotes "your ___ is great!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: 'A Canaanite woman from that region comes to Him.' / 'And friend, this is no polite little wave.' / 'She's CRYING OUT: ...' Only the opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: 'Not one word.' / 'Jesus stays silent.' / 'So His disciples come over to Him with a suggestion.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'So she's still crying out, and the disciples want her gone,' only restates what cards 6 to 8 already covered. Only 'Then Jesus speaks up' moves the passage forward.
The wrong answer 'coins' isn't the same kind of thing as 'crumbs' and 'bones'. Crumbs and bones are scraps a dog could eat. Coins aren't, so the choice is really only between two answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: 'I've been around cookies my whole life' doesn't match his backstory. He spent years in the back of a junk drawer, away from any baking.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The question is just verse 28 with one word blanked out. It reads like a test item, not like Papa Dorin pausing mid-story to let the baker lean in.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: The answers aren't the same kind of thing. 'faith' is a quality of the woman, 'voice' is a body sound, and 'family' is a group of people. That makes the right answer easy to spot.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's humor is thin across the whole walkthrough. The only comic beats are 'no polite little wave', 'NOPE' and the mild crumbs line on card 16. Most story cards read as plain narration, and none of the lines would get a laugh a baker repeats to a friend.

rule.text: Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
